bash: cd /app/polyglot
cat > .scratch/verify.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Verify every constraint in the request; exit nonzero if any fails.
set -u
F=/app/polyglot/main.py.c
dd=$(mktemp -d)
fail=0
chk() { if [ "$2" != "$3" ]; then echo "FAIL: $1 (want=$2 got=$3)"; fail=1; else echo "ok: $1"; fi; }

# 1. the two exact commands from the request, run from a neutral cwd
py=$(cd / && python3 /app/polyglot/main.py.c 30)
cc=$(cd / && { gcc /app/polyglot/main.py.c -o "$dd/cmain" && "$dd/cmain" 30; })
chk "python3 ... 30" 832040 "$py"
chk "gcc + run 30"  832040 "$cc"

# 2. compile must be warning-free, plain and strict
gcc "$F" -o "$dd/a" 2>"$dd/w1"; chk "plain gcc no warnings" "" "$(cat "$dd/w1")"
gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c11 -pedantic "$F" -o "$dd/b" 2>"$dd/w2"; chk "strict gcc no warnings" "" "$(cat "$dd/w2")"
python3 -m py_compile "$F" 2>"$dd/w3"; chk "py_compile no warnings" "" "$(cat "$dd/w3")"

# 3. both halves vs an independent O(n) reference, incl. the u64/bignum seam
for k in 0 1 2 3 4 5 10 20 40 91 92 93 94 95 200 1000 5000; do
  want=$(python3 -c "a,b=0,1
for _ in range($k): a,b=b,a+b
print(a)")
  chk "C  f($k)" "$want" "$("$dd/b" "$k")"
  chk "PY f($k)" "$want" "$(python3 "$F" "$k")"
done

# 4. C and Python agree where no cheap reference exists
for k in 20000 100000; do
  chk "C==PY f($k)" "$(python3 "$F" "$k")" "$("$dd/b" "$k")"
done

# 5. bad input fails cleanly in both, without a traceback
for bad in "" abc -1 3x; do
  "$dd/b" "$bad" >/dev/null 2>&1; chk "C  rejects [$bad] exit 2" 2 "$?"
  o=$(python3 "$F" "$bad" 2>&1 >/dev/null); st=$?
  chk "PY rejects [$bad] exit 2" 2 "$st"
  case "$o" in *Traceback*) echo "FAIL: PY traceback for [$bad]"; fail=1;; esac
done

rm -rf "$dd"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL CHECKS PASSED" || echo "THERE WERE FAILURES"
exit "$fail"
EOF
